# Clockspeed - Ledger

**Section status: HISTORICAL.** Every section in this file is a record, so a dated
heading here may mark its own section historical.

**Append-only, NEWEST FIRST. One record per closed work item.**

**This file owns:** the per-item completion record - what closed, when, and how to verify
it independently.

**This file never contains:** rules, open work, aspirational items, or architecture. Open
work lives in `ROADMAP.md`, aspirational work in `BACKLOG.md`, externally blocked work in
`docs/GATED.md`, and settled decisions in `docs/adr/` plus the `Settled` section of
`CLAUDE.md`.

Nothing in this file is ever edited or deleted once written. A record that turns out to
be wrong gets a **new, later** record that corrects it and says so. Pruned records move
to `docs/history_notes.md`; they are never dropped.

---

## Entry shape

Newest entry goes directly under the `## Entries` heading. Each entry is:

```
### 2026-09-13 - CS-1005 - CLOSED. The scope and the claim store were both correct and nothing in the driver path imported either

**WHAT CHANGED.** `ops/loop/queue_loop.py` now binds the row a cycle works to the row the lane may
work. `scope.lane_permit` computes the permitted ids BEFORE the cycle, so a cycle that closes its own
row cannot read as out-of-scope. `ClaimWatch` samples inside the poll loop as well as after the wait,
and the in-loop sample is load-bearing: a compliant worker releases at the wrap, so a post-cycle read
learns nothing from exactly the cycles that behaved. Binding is by set membership, the verdict is
written on every cycle, and the roll-up refuses `ok` when a row was worked outside the permit.

**PROVEN BY.** `tests/ops/test_scope_binding.py::test_a_row_outside_the_permit_reaches_the_record_and_refuses_the_roll_up`,
killed by four independent mutations including the checkout-local rooting that defeated two other
slices today. Merged files: `ops/loop/queue_loop.py`, `ops/loop/scope.py`.

**CLAIMS RATHER THAN COMMITS ARE THE SOURCE, and the reason is recorded so it is not simplified
later:** a worker fast-forwards its tree, so a sibling lane's commits land in the same revision
range. A claim record carries its lane; a commit does not.

**WHAT REMAINS PROSE, stated as plainly as the defect was.** A cycle that never claims cannot be
checked: it records itself unobserved and does NOT refuse `ok`. That clause was declined on
measurement rather than omitted - no worker claims today, so taking it would report every cycle of
every night unbound on the night it shipped. Filed as part of CS-1009's territory.

### 2026-09-13 - CS-992 - CLOSED. A second lane can start, and one lane still excludes itself

**WHAT CHANGED.** The roster carries more than one lane, the driver mutex name is DERIVED per lane
rather than the box-wide constant, and the lock slot varies per lane. Merged files:
`ops/loop/lanes.py`, `ops/loop/queue_loop.py`, `ops/loop/launch_queue_loop.ps1`.

**PROVEN BY.** `tests/ops/test_multi_lane.py::test_a_roster_insertion_cannot_hide_a_live_holder`.
The merger reproduced the pre-repair defect against the pre-repair candidate as a control - roster
insertion made `lane_state` read FREE while a live worker held the slot, and a second claim
succeeded - and the same probe on the repair reads RUNNING and refuses.

**THREE DEFECTS WERE FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE THIS CLOSED, each worth its fence.** The first cut
FOLDED lane names, so two distinct lanes collapsed onto one mutex - the defect the item exists to
prevent, arriving through the sanitiser; closed with a digest of the raw name. The second keyed lock
slots POSITIONALLY by roster index, so inserting a lane at the front re-pointed every slot; a lock is
now resolved by the lane its payload RECORDS. And scoping the mutex by repo token introduced a SAFETY
REGRESSION the acceptance never asked for - two clones at different paths got disjoint mutexes AND
disjoint locks while both pointed at one checkout, which the old box-wide constant had prevented by
accident. A box-wide guard keyed on the working directory alone now sits inside the per-lane one.

**A CORRECTED CLAIM.** An arm named for driver exclusion asserted the OPPOSITE of Win32: mutex
ownership is per-THREAD, so the same-thread nesting it measured was a statement about the stand-in,
which is stricter than the primitive. It now runs over the real mutex on two threads.

**UNVERIFIED, labelled rather than rounded up:** cross-PROCESS exclusion on the derived names.

### 2026-09-13 - CS-991 - NOT A COMPLETION RECORD. CS-991 STAYS OPEN, BLOCKED ON CS-1009. The claim store is built and its headline claim is in doubt under real use

**CS-991 STAYS OPEN and this entry does not close it.** Its acceptance says a row taken by one lane
is not takeable by another FOR THE LIFE OF THAT CYCLE. CS-1009 questions exactly that: the store
decides HELD against the pid recorded in the claim, and an LLM worker reaches python through a fresh
subprocess per call, so the claiming process exits immediately and the record reads RECLAIMABLE from
that moment. The arms pass; the calling convention may defeat them.

**WHAT MERGED.** `ops/loop/claims.py` keys claims by the ROW ID, never by queue index, line number or
slot - those reorder on every close, and a record keyed by one would re-point when a row above it
closed. A claim is resolved by the row its payload RECORDS, not by its file name. Proven by
`tests/ops/test_row_claim.py::test_a_second_lane_offered_the_same_queue_takes_a_different_row` and
`::test_a_crashed_cycle_does_not_release_its_claim`, the latter using `os._exit` so no `finally`,
`atexit` or `__exit__` runs.

**THE FIRST CUT SHIPPED A DEFECT WORSE THAN NO FEATURE, and the arm that should have caught it
assumed it away.** The store rooted itself at the importing FILE, and each lane's worker runs in its
OWN checkout, so the two lanes read different directories and were structurally blind to each other -
an adversary reproduced both lanes holding one row across two real processes. The arm written to
prove exclusion had passed an explicit shared root, so it could never see a defect that IS the root.
`lanes.REPO_ROOT` already resolved the indirection and the store now uses it. The merger verified
from a REAL git worktree, which is stronger than the arm, whose checkouts are synthetic.

**THE DRIVER-SIDE / WORKER-SIDE ASYMMETRY IS THE GENERAL LESSON** and is recorded in the module:
driver-side state may use the checkout because the driver runs from the main tree; WORKER-side state
may not, because each lane worker runs in its own worktree. Two independent slices got this wrong in
one session.

### 2026-09-13 - CS-993 - A FROZEN-FILE GRANT, GRANTED BY THE OPERATOR AND LEFT UNSPENT. Nothing was edited under it, and the reason is recorded so neither the grant nor the route it covers is re-pitched

**CS-993 STAYS OPEN and this entry does not close it.** Its acceptance says two lanes cannot run a
suite simultaneously, and two of the three pytest invocations in a cycle remain outside the ration -
including the only one that forks. What merged is the driver-side half, and the detection route that
addresses the remaining harm is filed as CS-1007.

**THE GRANT EXISTS AND IS NOT SPENT.** The operator granted the exception on
`.githooks/pre-push` in as many words. An adjudicator that wrote no part of CS-993, the hook or
either prior grant then ruled DENY on the EDIT, and the grant is recorded here GRANTED AND UNSPENT
rather than quietly dropped. That is the CS-972 shape on this same file: a grant issued, no edit ever
made, because conditions could not be honestly met. **A grant is permission, not a design.**

**THE GAP IS REAL AND WAS VERIFIED, not taken on the requester's word.** The hook's pytest
invocation carries `-n auto --dist loadfile` and is the ONLY xdist run in a lane cycle. CS-993
therefore covers none of the runs that fork, which is the mechanism the defect statement names. The
requester reported that honestly and routed the proposal rather than taking the edit.

**GROUND ONE - NO CEILING VALUE IS BOTH USEFUL AND SAFE.** A hook that waits usefully must wait at
least one suite; at the shipped ceiling constant it would wait three hours. The hook's OWN header
already rules on that scenario in as many words - a hung gate reads as a wedged suite and gets killed
rather than diagnosed, which is worse than either answer. A ceiling short enough to be safe on an
operator's interactive push falls through unrationed on essentially every real collision, making the
ration decorative. The hook cannot tell a lane push from an interactive one: it reads exactly one
environment variable, and CS-972's record already ruled that adding another IS ITSELF a frozen edit.

**GROUND TWO - THE ONLY WORKING MECHANICS ARE FROZEN-FILE LAUNDERING.** `sh` cannot hold a Python
context manager across a later command. The split form - acquire, run, release - records the
ACQUIRING process's pid, which is dead before pytest starts, so the slot reads reclaimable at once
and the next lane takes it: it would ration nothing while logging that it did. The only shape that
works inserts a wrapper between the gate and pytest, and the hook's own prose names that shape as the
CS-703 mechanism that turns all three tier-0 gates into no-ops. It would also move the gate's
exit-code fidelity into a NON-FROZEN module editable without any grant at all. Disqualifying on its
own.

**NAMED AND REJECTED SO IT IS NOT RE-PITCHED AS CHEAP.** Injecting a ration plugin through
`PYTEST_ADDOPTS` in the worker's environment reaches the hook's pytest with no frozen byte changed.
It is rejected: it fails OPEN AND SILENT if the variable is lost anywhere along the driver, worker,
git and hook chain, which is precisely the defect the ration exists to close, and it adds an
environment-variable disarm surface to a tier-0 gate.

**THE ROUTE THAT IS TAKEN INSTEAD IS DETECTION IN THE DRIVER, NOT PREVENTION IN THE GATE.** The harm
is not the overlap; it is an unattended lane writing a green it did not earn. The driver already
writes its ration verdict on every cycle and already refuses the cycle roll-up on an unrationed step.
Extending that to OBSERVE whether a foreign suite ran during the window it already polls converts an
unearned green into a re-run, costs no wait, hangs no push, and needs no grant. Filed as CS-1007.

**A FALSE CLAIM IN THE MERGED CODE WAS CORRECTED IN THE SAME CHANGE.** `ration`'s module docstring
quoted its coverage as one of three invocations as though that were unconditional. It holds only when
the driver is asked for a local suite; the flag defaults to false, so on a default night the driver
issues no suite and the ration covers zero of the two invocations that do run. The conditional was
written correctly at the call site and wrongly in the summary, which is the half a reader sees.

**ONE THING CS-993 MAKES WORSE, NARROWLY AND IN THE FAIL-CLOSED DIRECTION**, recorded rather than
smoothed over: an unrationed but green suite now sets the cycle row not-ok, an outcome that did not
exist before. That is the intended trade - an unmeasurable run should not read as an earned one - but
it is a new way for a night to report failure.

`shell/test/supervisor.test.js` and `shell/test/tray.test.js`.

**IT HAD NEVER BEEN EXECUTED.** `shell/node_modules` did not exist at session
start and every check in `docs/OPERATIONS.md` section 8.3 read `NOT RUN`. Five of

**A RUNBOOK DEFECT MEASURED, NOT REASONED.** The pinned Electron ships NO `scripts`
block, so `npm install` completes in about half a second having fetched no binary
and exits 0. The runtime downloads lazily on the first `require`. Section 8.1 said

**FIVE REFUTATIONS OF THE FIRST ROUND, by one adjudicator and three adversaries
that wrote none of it.** Each is repaired in `8777a89`.

1. **A local code-execution vector.** `main.js` spawned the bare name `python`

   environment variable is set at neither machine nor user scope, so an Explorer

2. **A zombie.** With no tray, close correctly meant close, `window-all-closed`
   fired with quitting false, and merely HAVING registered that listener
   suppressed the default quit - leaving a process with no window, no tray and a
   live dashboard it had started.
3. **The tray guard tested the wrong proposition.** `new Tray()` handed an image
   that decodes to nothing does NOT throw; it returns an ordinary non-null Tray
   with an invisible icon.
4. **No single-instance lock.** Two launches produced two windows and two tray
   icons, and two writers on one `window-state.json` whose fixed-name partial file
   is opened truncating - an interleave publishes a zero-byte state file over a
   good one, falsifying `shell/lib/state.js`'s own atomicity header.
5. **The wiring arms did not grade.** Fifteen mutations, THIRTEEN SURVIVED. A seam
   was satisfiable from a string literal, from dead code, and both lib modules
   could be replaced by local fakes and never loaded while every arm stayed green.
   The only kill was a behaviour-preserving reformat.

**THE REPAIR BRIEF WAS ITSELF REFUTED, and the spike wins.** It asserted that
`shutil.which` excludes the current directory, making `scripts/make_cert.py` the
safe precedent. Measured on the pinned interpreter with the guard absent, it
returned a RELATIVE path to a planted file in the current directory. `make_cert.py`
carries the same exposure. Filed as **CS-910** rather than fixed inside a slice
that did not own it.

**A MEASUREMENT IN THE SOURCE THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE.** `PROBE_ATTEMPT_CEILING`
carried a recorded 2.217s-2.227s cold start and reasoned a margin from it. Measured
through the actually shipped path - electron, `net`, `waitForSurface` verbatim - it
is 0.46s to 0.53s, every sample answering on the first attempt. The ten-millisecond
spread over five samples was the signature of a fixed constant, not a process
start. The margin at the old ceiling was about twenty times, not the four and a
half claimed. The comment now separates measured from judged.

**A DECISION, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-ARGUED.** The health probe uses electron's
`net` rather than node's `https`. With a `ca` option holding the pinned certificate
`https` works under stock node and FAILS under electron, which builds its node
against BoringSSL: every probe returned `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE` while the
surface was demonstrably listening. Going through `net` also deletes a second trust
decision rather than moving it - net requests reach `setCertificateVerifyProc`, so
the probe and the page are pinned by one answer from `shell/lib/trust.js`. An
adversary confirmed the pin against an impostor certificate on the same host, and
separately confirmed that probing BEFORE the proc is installed poisons the network
service's verdict cache so the proc never fires. That ordering is load-bearing and
is graded by nothing.

**A CORRECTION THIS ENTRY OWES TO `8210a3c`'s OWN MESSAGE.** That message states
that section 8.3 checks 1 to 5 were observed. The file at that commit records only
checks 1 and 3; checks 2, 4 and 5 were genuinely observed but never written down.
`docs/GATED.md` names recording an unrun check as a result a failure class, and a
commit message claiming a file says something it does not is that failure wearing a
different hat. The tracked note at `docs/item_notes/phase6.md` was correct
throughout. Repaired in `8777a89`.

### YYYY-MM-DD - <ITEM-ID> - <one line: what closed>
Verification: <pointer>
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| Date | `YYYY-MM-DD`, the date the item actually closed. |
| Item ID | The permanent `CS-` ID from `ROADMAP.md`. Never invented at close time, never reused, never renumbered. |
| One line | What closed. One line. If it needs a paragraph it needs its own file and this line becomes a pointer to it. |
| Verification pointer | How someone else confirms it, independently, without asking you. Mandatory. |

An entry may add an `ADR:` line citing `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` when the item settled a
decision. An entry that closes a gated item states which external condition was met and
who or what observed it.

## The verification pointer - what makes one valid

**Cite the item ID, the merged file, and the test name. Do not cite the slice SHA.**

A ledger entry whose only evidence is a commit SHA is **fragile**. The reason is
mechanical, not stylistic: work is produced in worktree-isolated agent slices, and those
slice commits frequently do not survive the cherry-pick into the main line. The SHA in
the entry then refers to an object that is unreachable, or reachable but not the version
that shipped. The entry looks precise and verifies nothing.

The item ID, the merged file path and the test name all survive the merge, because they
are properties of the shipped tree rather than of the branch that produced it.

**Valid pointers**

- `tests/save/test_header.py::test_world_token_stable_across_reload`
- `clockspeed/solve/exact.py` plus `tests/solve/test_exact.py::test_no_float_in_path`
- `tools/drift_guard.py` red-then-green transcript recorded under the item ID
- A named CI job on the tier-1 lane, plus the file it asserts on

**Invalid pointers**

- A bare commit SHA
- "tests pass" or "CI green" with nothing named
- A count of tests with no file and no test name behind it
- A link to a transcript or a chat message

Counts are never restated here as prose. If a count is worth citing, cite the
machine-checked artifact that produces it.

### 2026-09-16 - CS-1095 addendum - NOT A COMPLETION RECORD. The section 14 licence gate, RUN against the vendored doc after the fact, and CLEARED

**WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS.** `docs/CHANNEL.md` was vendored on a direct operator
instruction and this tree's own `CONVENTIONS.md` section 14 gate was NEVER RUN against
it. That gap was found by a SIBLING rather than here: LL refused the same file at its own
licence gate on 2026-09-15 for naming no licence, no holder and no repository, and that
refusal applied to this copy exactly as it applied to the original. The sending tree
conceded the omission plainly - it had named a commit and called the tree public, and
public is a VISIBILITY, not a GRANT.

**THE GATE WAS RUN HERE, TRAP BY TRAP, AGAINST THE SOURCE REPOSITORY'S OWN FILES** rather
than against the sending tree's summary of them. Section 14's first trap is that a repo
can contradict itself and one source alone gives the wrong answer, so a summary could not
have discharged it.

- TRAP 1, self-contradiction: NONE. `LICENSE`, the README licence paragraph and `NOTICE`
  agree. The `LICENSE` carries a SCOPE OF THIS LICENSE block stating the grant covers the
  source code and the authored documentation, naming "the Markdown that describes them",
  and carving out only the third-party data under `data/`. `docs/CHANNEL.md` is authored
  documentation and is not under `data/`. The scope block states that it CONTROLS where a
  data file and the licence appear to conflict.
- TRAP 2, a holder who cannot relicense: NOT PRESENT. One holder, `Moonbeam`, named in
  both `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`, and the sending tree wrote the doc's bytes itself.
- TRAP 3, a licence naming NOBODY: NOT PRESENT. The copyright line is RENDERED, not a
  template: `Copyright 2026 Moonbeam` at `LICENSE` line 189. Read the line, not the name.
- TRAP 4, truncation: NOT PRESENT. 219 lines, the warranty clause present.
- TRAP 5, source-available: NOT PRESENT. Zero occurrences of Elastic, BUSL or an
  all-rights-reserved reservation in `LICENSE` or the README.

**VERDICT: CLEARED FOR VENDORING.** Apache-2.0 is permissive and one-way compatible with
this tree's outbound licence.

**THE OBLIGATION THAT SURVIVES THE CLEARANCE**, because a permissive licence is not an
absent one. Apache-2.0 section 4 asks a redistributor to retain the attribution. The
vendored file is BYTE-PINNED and carries no notice of its own, and this tree may not add
one to it - so the attribution is recorded in the section 4 topology row, which is
auto-loaded every turn, and here. There are no changes to state: the copy is byte-identical
and its digest is pinned by an arm.

**STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE NOTICED: the named holder is also this repository's own
commit identity.** The same operator owns both trees. That is not an exemption from the
gate and it did not shorten it - the gate was run as if the holder were a stranger, which
is the only way its result means anything - but a reader who spotted it later and found it
unmentioned would be right to discount the verdict.

**WHAT THIS ENTRY DOES NOT CLOSE.** Nothing. CS-1095 is already closed above; this records
a gate that should have run before that entry and did not. The lesson belongs with the
record: an operator instruction moves the DECISION, not the GATE, and this tree ran the
vendoring without noticing it had skipped one of its own.

### 2026-09-15 - CS-1087 - CLOSED. A token carried only by an unparseable header is matchable without parsing it

**WHAT CHANGED.** `clockspeed/save/header.py` gained `scan_framed_tokens` and
`scan_world_tokens`: a bounded raw-byte scan that recovers a world token from the FRAMING
the engine writes around it - a length prefix, `WORLD_TOKEN_LENGTH` characters of the
token alphabet, a terminator - without parsing the header at all. `tools/precommit_gate.py`
calls it when `read_header` refuses, inside the SAME `SAVE_HEADER_BUDGET_SECONDS` clock on
the same `started` value, reading at most `MAX_HEADER_BYTES`, over only the files
`MAX_SAVE_HEADER_FILES` already admitted. Recovered candidates pass through the same
`_matchable` filter a parsed token does. The frozen-file GRANT recorded before the edit
binds all of this; its clause 2 preferred exactly this limb of the acceptance, and the
exit-status limb was DENIED because `.githooks/pre-commit` maps every non-zero status to
BLOCKED, which is the wedge the item forbids.

**HOW TO VERIFY IT INDEPENDENTLY.** Build a synthetic save, corrupt the version prologue,
and drive the gate's real discovery: `read_header` refuses with
`UnsupportedHeaderVersionError` and `scan_world_tokens` returns the token. Overwrite the
same file wholesale and the scan returns nothing. The arms are graded with an unreadable
header ACTUALLY PRESENT beside a parseable sibling, on leak IDENTITY and never on the exit
code, and the reader is proven ALIVE - exactly one header reported unparseable, both
tokens leaking.

**WHAT THE GRADERS CHANGED, because the first cut was not the shipped one.** An
adjudicator sent the candidate back and an adversary refuted three further claims. The
candidate cap counted raw hits BEFORE de-duplication, so one value repeated to the cap
followed by a DIFFERENT value discarded the second; and `hits` was shared across both
framings, so a full narrow population starved the wide scan entirely. Both lost real
tokens. The cap now counts DISTINCT values with a per-framing budget, and its truncation
reaches the exit status BLOCKING with an anti-hollowing control that fails if the scan is
disabled. Separately, `scan_framed_tokens` bound the prefix BARE in its own frame - the
first bare holder of a save prefix in the module, where the parse path leaves only dotted
holders - and the arm claiming otherwise was blind to it BY CONSTRUCTION, monkeypatching
the very function that held the buffer. It now scrubs on its own unwind and the arm
refuses through a shipped inner function.

**THE RESIDUE, MEASURED AND NOT GLOSSED.** Recovery is 4 of 4 tokens PRESENT in the bytes,
but only 4 of 9 unreadable SHAPES. Five carry no recoverable token: truncated before the
identifier, truncated mid-identifier, overwritten wholesale, zero-byte, and a file that
cannot be opened at all. A sixth shape recovers nothing though the characters ARE on disk -
the identifier is intact behind a DAMAGED COUNT PREFIX, so the framing the scan keys on is
gone. On the live library this run: 31 files, 1 unreadable, and that one recovered NOTHING -
it is the truncated-before-the-identifier case. So the coverage limb is 0-for-1 on real
data today, which is a floor on this item's value and not a defect in it. CS-1083's cited
0-of-28 was re-measured as ordered by the grant and is now 1 of 31.

**ONE LABELLED RESIDUAL IN THE NEW BLOCKING PATH.** It differs in KIND from the five bounds
beside it: those trip on how many files the operator has, while this one trips on the
CONTENT of a single file the gate may never remove (non-negotiable 1), and its reason names
neither the value (grant clause 7) nor the file. If it ever fired, the only escape would be
`--no-verify` - the wedge this item exists to avoid, arriving by another door. Measured
probability is effectively nil: a real header carries about ten strings, and 16 DISTINCT
framed candidates of the measured length inside the byte bound is unreachable for random or
compressed bytes. It is recorded because it is a real difference, not because it is likely.

### 2026-09-15 - CS-1093 - CLOSED. The 7-bit walk names every offending module rather than the first

**WHAT CHANGED.** `test_every_module_this_split_created_is_seven_bit_ascii` in
`tests/test_bare_path_citations.py` asserted INSIDE its `for path in paths` loop, so the
first module carrying a byte above the 7-bit range short-circuited the walk and every
later offender stayed invisible until that one was repaired. That is the pooled-guard
shape this project has filed before: a guard that reports one member of a failing
population teaches the reader the damage is smaller than it is. The arm now collects
every offender and asserts once on the collected set. The missing-file case was folded
into the same collection rather than left as a second in-loop assert, which would have
re-introduced the short-circuit by another door.

**THE SCALAR BINDING IS THE POINT, NOT A STYLE CHOICE.** pytest's assertion rewriting
renders the asserted EXPRESSION independently of the message, so `assert not offenders`
prints the list whatever the message says - measured on the pre-repair arm, which printed
`assert not [195, 169]`. The count is bound to a plain scalar first and the assert reads
`offending_modules == 0`, so the rewriter renders `assert 2 == 0` and the names reach the
report only through the authored message.

**HOW TO VERIFY IT INDEPENDENTLY.** Append a non-ASCII byte to BOTH
`tests/archive_rot_guard.py` and `tests/bare_path_guard.py`, then run
`python -m pytest tests/test_bare_path_citations.py -k seven_bit`. The failure names BOTH
modules and renders `assert 2 == 0`. Snapshot the two files first and restore from the
snapshot, never with `git checkout`, which would discard uncommitted work. The plant
REPORTS rather than crashing because the walk reads bytes and never decodes, so no
UnicodeDecodeError can destroy the fixture - the failure mode that killed an equivalent
plant earlier in this project.

**WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** The walked population is the modules this split created, seven of
them, and not the whole tests tree. Widening it was not in the acceptance and was not done.

construction. The declination was adjudicated SOUND and is not being reversed: the module

reason, and it is non-negotiables 1 and 7.

are the precedent here.**

1. May change: the world-token discovery path, `_world_tokens_from_headers` and helpers it
   calls, for the sole purpose of making a token carried only by an unparseable header
   matchable WITHOUT parsing that header. Nothing else in the file.
2. THE PREFERRED REMEDY IS THE FIRST LIMB OF THE ACCEPTANCE - matchability without
   parsing - NOT the exit-status limb. Attempt it first. This is CS-1083 clause 2's shape:
   cover, do not signal.
3. A RAW-BYTE FALLBACK SCAN OF A BOUNDED PREFIX OF A `.sav` IS PERMITTED, and the read is
   not a new class of access. The gate already opens save files: `_world_tokens_from_headers`
   calls the header reader, and `read_header` in `clockspeed/save/header.py` does

   WRITING to the save directory and to the install; it has never forbidden reading, and
   `_save_root_dirs` already says so for the listing.
   The fallback opens `"rb"`, never any write or append mode, never `os.remove`, never a
   rename, never a temp file beside the save.
4. THE FALLBACK IS BOUNDED BY THE SAME CONSTANTS THAT ALREADY BOUND THE HEADER SCAN, and
   this is mandatory rather than advisory. It runs inside the same
   `SAVE_HEADER_BUDGET_SECONDS` aggregate wall clock, tested at the same point in the same
   loop, on the same `started` clock; it reads at most `MAX_HEADER_BYTES` per file; and it
   examines only files already admitted by `MAX_SAVE_HEADER_FILES`, itself derived from
   `MAX_SAVE_ROOT_ENTRIES`. No new budget constant is introduced, because a second budget
   is a second thing to drift. Per CS-1083 clause 3, no existing bound may be silently
   removed and `SAVE_HEADER_BUDGET_SECONDS` keeps a live refusal path.
5. THE HARVEST IS IDENTITY-CONSTRAINED, NEVER A GENERAL STRING SCRAPE. A candidate enters
   the blocklist only if it passes the token's own measured shape - `WORLD_TOKEN_LENGTH` in
   `clockspeed/save/header.py`, which `_warnings_for` in that module enforces - and
   then `_matchable` against `MIN_WORLD_TOKEN_CHARS` and `GENERIC_ACCOUNT_NAMES`, exactly
   as a parsed token does today. A scrape that admits arbitrary runs would add engine
   strings to a whole-word blocklist, and because clause 7 forbids ever naming the value,
   the operator gets an UNCLEARABLE false positive whose only remedy is `--no-verify` -
   which is the wedge this item exists to avoid, arriving by a different door.
6. THE RAW PREFIX IS SCRUBBED ON EVERY PATH, INCLUDING THE UNWIND. This is the one
   genuinely NEW exposure and the clause that matters most. Today the gate NEVER holds raw
   save bytes in a frame of its own: it delegates to `clockspeed/save/header.py`, whose
   CS-963 scrub inside `read_header` deletes the buffer before re-raising, with the comment "this
   frame holds a bounded PREFIX of the file, which is precisely the personal-data-bearing

   path, and never store it on an object that outlives the call.
7. NO DIAGNOSTIC, SKIP, COUNT LINE OR EXCEPTION MAY RENDER A SCANNED VALUE, and the
   existing design already holds this - MEASURED rather than assumed. `check_pii` builds
   its `Diagnostic` with a CONSTANT reason; `_discovered_rules` states the rule
   and its four reasons carry no value, the world-token one being "a world token

   returned unchanged; checked lines render label, origin and byte count; every

   BLOCKLIST THEREFORE CREATES NO ECHO PATH THAT DOES NOT ALREADY EXIST - the exposure is

8. Must NOT change, carrying CS-1083 clause 5 forward unaltered and adding two: a skip line

**WHY `.githooks/pre-commit` IS DENIED.** The second limb of the acceptance - a distinct
exit status - cannot be taken without it and cannot be taken safely with it. The hook maps
every non-zero status to BLOCKED and exits with it, so a third status BLOCKS until the
unreadable file is gone, on a file the gate may not remove (non-negotiable 1) and
intermittently on every autosave in flight (non-negotiable 7). Making that status advisory

of gate failure that no longer refuses - the CS-703 and CS-823 failure mode restated, in a
file whose whole body is the record of closing it. WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE FOR A GRANT:

header is shown unrecoverable from the raw prefix under clauses 4 and 5 - and the advisory
status shown, by a planted unrun and a planted truncated gate, not to weaken the CS-823

denial.

DETAIL.** CS-1083's own record shows why: its first cut HOLLOWED the CS-436 arms, which
then passed with world-token detection completely destroyed. A suppressed or monkeypatched

whether a token was recovered. The fixture is a synthetic `.sav` whose header genuinely
does not parse, carrying a synthetic token of the measured length, in a temporary save root

**THE UNPROVEN CLAUSE, NAMED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR A MEASURED ONE.** Nothing here
measures that a token IS recoverable from the raw prefix of a header that fails to parse -
that depends on where the parse fails, and a file truncated before the identifier carries

population, and the residue after this item is that part. Separately, the single

**THE DEFECT.** `tests/save/test_struct_interior.py::test_a_stricter_shared_ceiling_cannot_improve_this_modules_grade`

**ROOT CAUSE, and it is the ORDER of two lines rather than either line.** Evidence about a
restore the control owes has to be taken before the fixture's net closes. Once `undo()` has
run there is no reading left that could differ.

before `undo()`, and that reading is what the revert assertion grades. The post-undo
assertion is kept and its message now says what it is - the net, failing only if
`monkeypatch` itself stopped working. `_run_ceiling_control` grew one mutant seam,
`_CEILING_CONTROL_RESTORES`, guarding the trailing `_install_ceiling(original)` in its
record loop; at its default the path is behaviourally identical to the unconditional line
it replaced. The seam is in process and never on disk for the reason `_EarlyTerminator`
states next door: the harness Bash timeout kills rather than unwinds, so a mutation applied
to a tracked file can outlive the run that made it.

### 2026-09-14 - CS-1060 - CLOSED. Tier 1 went 583 seconds to a worst job of 310, by partition and trimming with no threshold touched - and the clause nearly closed on a reading of the runner pool that was backwards

**WHAT CHANGED.** `.github/workflows/tier1.yml` runs THREE jobs where it ran two. A new `guards`

fixed-cost claim still measures at 96, so the arm was not weakened to buy the time.

**MEASURED FIRST, AND THE OBVIOUS REPAIR WAS THE WRONG ONE.** The shard was bound by total CPU work
divided by worker count, not by any single slow file: 607.7 CPU-seconds locally against a 108.7s
wall, and 607.7 x 3.4 / 4 predicts 517s against the 540s the runner actually spent. So trimming the
largest test buys a QUARTER of its own cost in wall time. Only more runners move a lane shaped like
that, which is why the acceptance names partition first.

**M IS THE WORST JOB IN THE LANE, NOT THE JOB NAMED `fast`.** The ROADMAP line said "fast-shard",
which was shorthand from a session in which `fast` WAS the worst job. The detail file says "the
slow-class worst job reading" and `.github/workflows/tier1.yml` states a level "bounds the SLOWEST
SHARD and never their sum". Read literally the lane could satisfy the acceptance while the gate
stayed infeasible. **So M = 310s, the save shard. Margin against 320 is TEN SECONDS.**

**THE CLASS CAVEAT, STATED AS A PROBABILITY BECAUSE THAT IS ALL IT IS.** The slow runner class was
never observed directly and three readings alone would NOT have discharged this clause. The merger
believed the tight 43s spread meant the slow class had been missed. That was BACKWARDS, and an
adjudicator established it with a 49-reading class model built from 24 recent runs: the slow class
is roughly 78 per cent of draws, so P(all three readings being fast-class) is about 0.012 for both
the save and fast shards, and the three save readings sit at the MAXIMUM of a 22-reading
distribution whose dense band is 258 to 310. Re-measured independently by the merger: 158, 171, 217,
then nineteen readings from 258 to 310. A tight cluster at the top of that distribution is the slow
class, not an unsampled one.

**WHY THIS HAS ITS OWN ID INSTEAD OF CLOSING CS-448.** Read as plain text, CS-448's acceptance
disjunct (b) - "its nested child run is made robust against the contention that breaks it, with the
mechanism named rather than the timeout raised" - is satisfied word for word by this work. It was
routed to an adjudicator anyway and the adjudicator refused the reading, correctly. CS-448's own note under
its heading in `docs/item_notes/phase4.md` fixes the referent of "the contention": "xdist supplies only the
concurrent creator and deleter - it is NOT CPU contention, and the 42.7s walk happens single-process
with nothing else running", and the note ends with an explicit "Measure `rootdir` inside a real
tier-2 job before closing." Two different breakage signatures: CS-448's is `FileNotFoundError` into
an interrupted collection, this one is the windows leg crossing `_CHILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. Bounding a
child at four workers does nothing whatsoever to a rootdir that climbs. **AN ACCEPTANCE READ WITHOUT
ITS NOTE IS HOW AN ITEM CLOSES ON A MECHANISM IT NEVER NAMED.** CS-448 stays open on its rootdir
measurement, which nobody has taken.

**WHAT CHANGED.** `tests/save/test_phase4_gate.py::_child_pytest_args` appends
`-n <bounded> --dist loadfile`, with `_CHILD_WORKERS = min(4, max(2, os.cpu_count() or 2))`. No
timeout moved; `_CHILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is 300 before and after.

**THE CAP IS MEASURED, NOT PREFERRED.** Same tree, same box, `--dist loadfile`, 1197 passed and 96
skipped at every point: serial 68.98s, `-n 2` 46.68s, `-n 4` 37.72s, `-n 8` 33.41s, `-n 16` 33.96s.
Sixteen workers are SLOWER than eight - under `loadfile` the critical path is the slowest single
FILE, and `test_absolute_claims.py`'s top-five durations alone are 29.6s of the 69 serial seconds.
Four workers take 87.9 per cent of the whole available gain at a quarter of the process count, and
on the 4-core windows runner the cap does not bind at all. A serial control re-run after the sweep
read 69.25s against the opening 68.98s, so the box did not drift under the measurement.

**`--dist load` WAS FASTER AND WAS DECLINED.** 32.68s at n=4. `.github/workflows/tier1.yml` runs
`tests/save` under `loadfile`, so that is the only mode a lane has ever run this directory in. Five

`tests/save` run the child cost 39.41s against 15 competing parent workers, versus 37.37s unopposed.
That degradation under a filled box is the property the serial child did not have.

**PROVEN BY.** `tests/save/test_phase4_gate.py::test_the_child_run_asks_for_bounded_parallelism_rather_than_auto`,

### 2026-09-14 - CS-869 - CLOSED. The ceiling control's strength is derived from the corpus and its skip is keyed on what the plant moves

**THE DEFECT, AND IT WAS TWO HALVES OF ONE SENTENCE.** The third anti-monotone control in
`tests/save/test_struct_interior.py` planted a tag ceiling of 8 - a bare literal - and then decided
whether the plant was worth grading by comparing STRUCT SITE totals. A tag ceiling refuses whole
RECORDS: the walk runs out of iterations and reports nothing. A refused record costs a struct site
only when it happened to carry one, so on every ceiling whose refusals land on struct-free records
the site totals matched, the skip fired, and the arm left before reaching either assertion that
catches a shared constant moving this module's own reading. The item measured the suppression
directly: with CS-863's defect restored, one such ceiling gave 1 skipped at exit 0 where the shipped
literal gave 1 failed at exit 1.

**THE ROOT CAUSE** is that the skip and the plant were keyed on different quantities, and the
literal is what hid it - a number picked against one corpus sat where the corpus's own shape
belonged, and its docstring's claim that any ceiling below the observed maximum exercised the same
loss class was measured false by the item before this cycle started.

**WHAT CHANGED.** `_CEILING_CONTROL_TAGS` is gone. `_derive_ceiling_control_tags` returns the middle
of the corpus's own tags-per-payload distribution, clamped into the band the control requires, and
declines outright when the deepest payload admits no ceiling both above one and below it - so the
control says it has nothing to plant rather than planting a kill. `_CEILING_CONTROL_FLOOR` remains a
BAND EDGE and is not a second picked strength. The distribution comes from `_StructSweep`, which is
cached and which the arm already pays for, so nothing re-reads a library the operator is playing
into. The arm now ASSERTS the corpus exceeds what it installed, which is the half the old literal
had nothing checking. `_the_plant_cost_nothing` is the skip, and it forgives only a plant that took
neither a record nor a site.

**AND ONE ASSERTION THAT COULD NOT REPORT WHAT ITS MESSAGE NAMED WAS REPLACED RATHER THAN KEPT.**
The old strict fall in struct sites said a failure meant the plant had cost the shipped reader
nothing measurable, and it sat directly below a skip that had already left on exactly that equality,
so that case was never its to report. IT WAS NOT UNFIREABLE, and the looser claim is corrected here
rather than left standing: a plant that made the shipped walk find MORE would still have failed it.
Two monotonicity assertions stand there now and cover that direction in both quantities - a stricter
ceiling cannot find more sites and cannot open more records - and the anti-monotone site check is
asked only where a site was actually lost, because demanding one on a corpus whose refusals are all
struct-free would redden a healthy tree for the shape of its library.

**PROVEN BY.** `tests/save/test_struct_interior.py::test_the_ceiling_controls_skip_forgives_only_a_plant_that_cost_nothing`
and `::test_the_ceiling_controls_strength_is_derived_from_the_corpus`. Both are SYNTHETIC and
deterministic - they grade the decision and never the library, so they redden on a machine with no

### 2026-09-14 - CS-302 - CLOSED. The refusal diagnosis cost one full elimination per row, and it was measured at live scale before it was replaced

**WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND.** `ratio._name_unsatisfiable_item` recovered the name of the
unsatisfiable item by dropping one row at a time and re-solving, which is one full exact
elimination PER ROW on top of the solve that already refused. The item's own note recorded
that as reasoned acceptable for optimizer-sized sets and NOT measured at real scale. Measured
now, against the registry this machine's install actually builds - 750 items, 872 recipes, 0
recipes excluded - the system the whole recipe set produces WITH ONE TARGET ON IT is 750 rows
by 872 columns under `BYPRODUCT_BALANCED` and 153 by 872 under `BYPRODUCT_SINKABLE`. The
target matters to the second number and not the first, and saying so is a correction: under
`sinkable` an unconsumed byproduct gets no equation, so the same recipe set with NO target is
152 by 872 and naming one of those 598 sunk items as the target is what adds the row. Under
`balanced` every one of them already carries a balance row, so the count does not move. One `solve_linear` over the
balanced system takes 4.86 s and one leave-one-out probe over it takes 4.73 s, so the loop's
worst case of 750 probes is 3549 s - 59 minutes to explain a refusal the solve itself reached
in under five seconds. The sinkable system's 153 probes are 193.6 s. NOT ACCEPTABLE, so the
diagnosis was replaced rather than blessed.

The 3549 s is one measured probe times the loop's own bound and not a wall-clock run of all
750; the loop is a `for` over `range(len(system.rows))` and the bound is therefore exact,
but this entry says which half was measured so the number is not read as a stopwatch reading.

**WHAT REPLACED IT.** `clockspeed/solve/exact.py` gains `isolating_rows`, which answers the
same question in ONE elimination. The elimination carries the transform that produced it, so
every row whose coefficients vanish is a left null vector `y` of the matrix in original row
order and the constant beside it is `y . rhs`. Those vectors are a basis of the left null
space `N`, because the accumulated transform is a product of elementary operations and is
therefore invertible. Writing `f(y) = y . rhs`, striking row `i` leaves `N_i = {y in N :
y[i] == 0}` and the reduced system is consistent exactly when `f` vanishes on `N_i` - which,
since `N_i` and `ker f` both have codimension at most one in `N`, happens exactly when the
coordinate functional `y -> y[i]` is a NONZERO multiple of `f` on `N`. That is a column
comparison against the constants, not a solve. Measured on the same balanced system:
8.94 s against the loop's 3549 s, a factor of 397. On the sinkable system, 1.48 s against
193.6 s, a factor of 131.

**THE VERIFIER REFUTED ONE OF THESE ARMS AND IT IS REPAIRED HERE.** The arm named for the
empty answer was pointed at the wrong system: `x + y = 1`, `y + z = 1`, `x + z = 1` against
`x + y + z = 2` is contradicted as a SET, and striking any one of those rows leaves a system
that HAS a solution - so every index is isolating and the arm was measuring `(0, 1, 2, 3)`
while its name and its docstring both said empty. It passed anyway, because its only
assertion was equality with the oracle. That is the lesson worth keeping: an arm whose whole
claim is delegated to an oracle cannot notice it is aimed at the wrong subject. The empty case
is now two independent contradictions over disjoint variables, it asserts the empty tuple
DIRECTLY as well as against the oracle, and the original fixture is kept under a name that
says what it does - it is the only one here whose answer is every row.

**THE EQUIVALENCE IS PROVEN AGAINST THE LOOP ITSELF, NOT ASSERTED.** The replaced loop is
written out again in `tests/solve/test_exact.py` as `_brute_force_isolating` and used as an
ORACLE. `test_isolating_rows_answers_exactly_what_the_leave_one_out_loop_answered` runs both
over a 240-seed corpus, 227 of which are inconsistent, and requires the answers to be equal
index for index. The corpus is dense with rows that are exact scalar multiples of earlier
rows, deliberately: that is what drives the left null space above one dimension, and a
criterion that works when the contradiction has a single witness is not the same as one that
works. Two mutations were planted and both were killed by that arm - dropping the nonzero
clause from the multiple test, and letting a zero-constant basis vector stop constraining.

**THE COST CLAIM IS A COUNT AND NEVER A CLOCK.** A wall-clock bound asserted in the suite
would be a statement about the machine that ran it and would pass on a fast enough machine
against the implementation this item replaced. Both cost arms count elimination passes at
`exact._validate_system`, which every entry point that eliminates calls exactly once before
touching a coefficient. `test_isolating_rows_does_not_grow_its_work_with_the_row_count` pins
one pass at 6 rows and one at 96, and requires the ORACLE's cost to grow between those two
sizes so the arm cannot quietly become a comparison of two constants.

**SIBLING SWEEP: ONE SITE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POPULATION.** `grep` for the drop-and-resolve
shape over `clockspeed/` returns exactly `ratio.py:644`, and `solve_linear` has no other
caller in the package that loops. Nothing else to sweep, which is reported rather than
assumed.

**THE ZERO-WIDTH SHAPE IS GRADED BECAUSE `ratio.py` BUILDS IT.** With every selected recipe
excluded there is no variable, so there is no column, and what is left is a demand with nothing
on the other side. Those rows carry no coefficients at all, every one of them is trivially a
left null vector, and the whole question falls to the constants - the thinnest the criterion
ever gets. Five such systems are held to the oracle. The empty system is held to a written
answer INSTEAD of the oracle, and that is deliberate: the oracle calls a row isolating when
removing it leaves a consistent system, which every row of an already-consistent system
satisfies vacuously, so it is an oracle for inconsistent systems only and is guarded as one
everywhere it is used.

**BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED, INCLUDING THE FALLBACK.** The cheap all-zero-row check still runs
first and still returns the first such row. When no single row isolates the contradiction -
three or more mutually dependent rows - `isolating_rows` returns empty and the caller still
names the first balance row, because a refusal with no subject is one nobody can act on. The
three refusals the suite already pinned name the same items they named before, and that was
re-derived rather than assumed: the old loop and the new code were both run against the real
`_System` each of the three builds, and all three agree on the item.

**THE FALLBACK IS UNCHANGED AND IS STILL NOT REACHED BY ANY TEST THROUGH THE CALLER**, which
the verifier measured rather than inferred - a `trace` run over `tests/solve/test_ratio.py`
puts zero hits on that return while the fast path takes two and the isolating branch four.
It is reachable: a system from the corpus generator drives it, and it names the first row as

is FILED as CS-1067 rather than closed here - `isolating_rows` returning empty is now cheap to

### 2026-09-14 - CS-301 - CLOSED. The variable-power law was unmeasured, not unmeasurable, and the obvious cross-check was wrong

**WHAT CHANGED.** `clockspeed/solve/power.py` gains `bounded_draw`, which answers the two shapes
that declare no scalar with two exact `Fraction` bounds at the reference clock. The variable shape
takes its bounds from the recipe through the law ADR 0021 measured - minimum is the constant,
maximum is the constant plus the factor - and the struct-range shape reads both bounds off the
declaration and consults no recipe. Before this, all four of those buildings reported unmodeled and
contributed nothing to a power plan.

**THE REFUSAL WAS CORRECT AND ITS PREMISE WAS NOT.** The item note said the semantics of
`mVariablePowerConsumptionConstant` and `mVariablePowerConsumptionFactor` were unmeasured anywhere in
this project. True when written, and it was read for a year as though it meant unmeasurable. ADR 0020
had since made the publisher's own headers queryable; the two members carry doc comments stating the
law in as many words, and `clockspeed/data/assets.py` found them in an index of 8024 reflected
property declarations. The lesson is the note's shape rather than its content: a refusal recorded
without the condition that would lift it reads as a permanent verdict.

**THE FIRST IMPLEMENTATION WAS WRONG AND THE DOCUMENT CAUGHT IT.** The obvious cross-check is that
the recipe's two numbers EQUAL the estimated range declared on the building. That was written,
tested green against the synthetic corpus, and then measured against the shipped document, where it
holds on 25 of 25 recipes for one building, 6 of 6 for a second, and 0 of 12 for the third, whose
recipes carry two distinct bands. The building estimate is the ENVELOPE over its recipes, not any one
of them: taking the minimum constant and the maximum constant-plus-factor across each building's own
recipes reproduces its declared range on 3 of 3. So the published check is CONTAINMENT, and it holds
on 43 of 43 real pairings. It is not vacuous - asked against the pairings the document does not
declare, it rejects 1705 of 2573.

**WHAT IS STILL NOT PUBLISHED.** No scalar. The instantaneous draw rides `mPowerConsumptionCurve`, a
`UCurveFloat` asset the docs document does not export, so the cycle average is unknown and
`BoundedDraw` has no field that could hold one - the same fence `ClockCeiling` carries.

operands are per recipe and the envelope they are checked against is per building, and the two
pairings now return different outcomes in one test.

pairs, and the graded pair (60,14) led the next by 3538 records against a 7739-record

READER reads it correctly - 400 of 400 sampled records. The module's own independent tag

`tests/repr_rendering_guard.py` loses the `UnlockState` exemption.

**WHY THE FIRST CANDIDATE WAS REFUSED, AND IT IS THE FINDING OF THE ITEM.** It keyed
`UNLOCK_CARRIERS` on C++ DECLARING class names - `AFGSchematicManager` and siblings - taken
from the install's headers. A save is joined on the SAVE-SIDE type path, which UE writes
without the A/U prefix and with a `BP_*_C` spelling for a blueprint carrier. Not one key
matched. The reader would have matched ZERO records on every real save while every
synthetic arm passed. A whole-suite run of 3153 tests went GREEN over that tree. The suite
could not see it, and that is a measurement about the suite rather than about the code.

**THE REASONING ERROR THAT PRODUCED IT IS THE REUSABLE PART.** ADR 0016 was found to carry
two false statements, and that was taken as licence to prefer the headers over the ADR
wholesale. It is not. A header declaration answers WHAT C++ DECLARES; the save answers WHAT
IS IN THE FILE; for save contents the save is ground truth, and the ADR's carrier table is a
measurement over real saves. **A document with false statements in it is not a document with
no true measurements in it.** The wrong keys were handed to the builder by an item note
which also said DO NOT RE-VERIFY. The note has been corrected and now leads with that
correction.

**WHAT THE REPAIR ADDED THAT THE ORIGINAL LACKED.** Fixtures now parse ADR 0016's carrier
table AT TEST TIME, so fixture and oracle no longer share a source, and a control arm
asserts every production key is reachable from that table. Mutating a key back to the
declaring-class spelling now reddens. Removing the `UnlockState` repr exemption made
`test_no_shipped_class_renders_a_graded_field` able to see the type at all - under the
retained exemption, deleting `__repr__` stayed green.

**A MASKED CLAUSE WAS FOUND AND FIXED INSIDE THE GUARD.** Deleting the separator check left
all three guard arms green: the attack path did not begin with a permitted root, so the root
check refused it first and the two clauses were never told apart. A second fixture wearing a
permitted root, refusable only by the separator, now separates them, plus an assertion that
it still passes the root check so the masking cannot silently return.

**WHAT IS NOT DONE, RECORDED AS NOT DONE.** `mTradingPostLevel` is unwired. ADR 0016
records no carrier type path for it, and keying it would mean inventing a class name - the
exact defect that refused the first candidate. It stays in `UNLOCK_CARRIERS_UNREAD`, the
field stays `None`, the unread warning still fires, and the clause is re-sited to CS-1052
with its evidence bar RAISED to a measurement against a real save. Rewriting the acceptance
to match the delivery was refused outright.

**OVERLAP WITH CS-913, RECORDED SO TWO ITEMS DO NOT CLAIM ONE CHANGE.** `ROADMAP.md`'s
CS-913 line requires `current_game_phase` be retyped off `int | None` because the value is
an asset reference. This item delivered that retype, because its own acceptance forced it.
CS-913 remains OPEN for everything else it names, and whoever takes it must not re-file the
retype as undone.

**RESIDUAL RISK, CARRIED FORWARD AS CS-1053.** The independence restored was from the item
note only. ADR 0016 is now the single source for BOTH production keys and fixtures, is still
`proposed`, and carries two statements already measured false. The reader is correct by
citation, not correct by measurement.

### 2026-09-13 - CS-1009 - CLOSED. A claim now survives the exit of the process that made it, and three designs were refuted before one held

**THE DEFECT, REPRODUCED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS DESIGNED.** `_state_of` decided HELD against the pid
recorded in the claim. A worker reaches python through a fresh subprocess per call, so the claiming
process exits at once and the row read RECLAIMABLE for the rest of a cycle that runs for thousands of
seconds. Measured with two real processes and a control on the same tree: the long-lived holder read
HELD and refused a second lane, the claimant that exited read RECLAIMABLE and a second lane CLAIMED
THE ROW. That is the double-booking CS-991 exists to stop, restored by the calling convention.

**WHAT CHANGED.** Liveness DELEGATES to the lane lock of the lane the record itself names, matched on
the run id the store READS OFF THAT LOCK rather than accepts from its caller - `launch_lane` never
hands the worker the driver's run id, so a caller-supplied one would have mismatched on every real
fire and answered RECLAIMABLE for every claim. The lock directory is derived from the claim root, so a
worker importing its own checkout's copy still anchors on the main tree. Ownership for release is
DERIVED too: `running_cycle_here` matches the checkout the module was imported from against the
worktree each lane lock records, and no credential crosses a subprocess boundary at all. Merged files:
`ops/loop/claims.py`, `ops/loop/lanes.py`, `tools/headless-queue.md`, `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.

**PROVEN BY.** `tests/ops/test_row_claim.py::test_a_claim_outlives_the_process_that_made_it_while_its_cycle_runs`
and `::test_a_genuinely_dead_cycle_returns_its_row`, with
`::test_a_live_cycle_holds_its_row_however_old_the_record_is` fencing the age floor the acceptance
forbids by name - an inserted `age_s > 3600` floor reddens five arms. A second, independent
reproduction by an adversary that did not build it: the old tree double-books, the new tree refuses
`row_claimed`, and removing the lane lock flips the same probe to `RECLAIMABLE/pid`, which is the
control that separates graded-clean from graded-nothing.

**THREE RELEASE DESIGNS WERE REFUTED, AND THE PATTERN IS THE FINDING.** A caller-supplied `run_id` was
refuted because run ids are policed nowhere - two live claims under the identical string both
succeeded, `""` was accepted, `None` became the string `"None"` - so a crashed cycle's late wrap
deleted the live holder's record with NO malicious actor and both sides following the documented
convention. A sha256 RECEIPT over the record's bytes was refuted because every lane can read every
claim file, so the attacker recomputed it in one line - and re-hashing was the ONLY recovery path the
worker prompt left a cycle that lost the string, so the convention steered a worker into the attack.
What held was removing the credential entirely: an attacker derives its own lane, finds a record
naming another, and refuses structurally rather than by comparing a string it could compute. EVERY
CREDENTIAL A READER OF THE PROTECTED OBJECT CAN CONSTRUCT IS NOT A CREDENTIAL.

**AN ADJUDICATOR RULED THE ANCHOR FORK, and the ruling is why the provability gate is not on the state
path.** A repair that required a lock to PROVE its holder before anchoring a claim was measured to
invert the item where `proc_started` cannot read - unconditionally without psutil, which
`pyproject.toml` declares optional, and on this box through `psutil.AccessDenied` for an elevated or
scheduled-task driver - handing a LIVE cycle's row to the other lane. The ruling was strict
delegation, on the ground that `lanes.holder_is_a_stranger` already decided this exact trade one layer
down: freeing a lane on a guess is strictly worse than the wedge, and a row is a smaller unit than a
lane, so the ranking cannot invert going up. The cost is disclosed rather than hidden:
`ANCHOR_LANE_UNPROVEN` is a declared third reading, and `docs/OPERATIONS.md` section 11 documents the
operator's escape - clear the stale lane lock, never the claim record.

**A FOURTH BREACH WAS FOUND AFTER THE SUITE WENT GREEN.** Two lane locks recording ONE worktree made
`running_cycle_here` resolve by roster order, so `LANES[0]` won every time: the other lane could not
release its own records and could delete the first lane's live one by naming the public row id.
`claims.py` ASSERTED that no two lanes share a worktree and nothing enforced it. Repaired on both
sides - `lanes.try_acquire_lane` refuses a worktree another lane's live lock records, and an ambiguous
checkout now derives NO lane rather than a guess. Proven by
`::test_a_second_lane_is_refused_a_worktree_another_lane_is_running_in`,
`::test_an_ambiguous_checkout_derives_no_lane_rather_than_the_first_one` and
`::test_a_lane_sharing_a_worktree_cannot_delete_the_other_lanes_record`.

**VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AT THE MERGED SHA.** 7269 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed, exit code read from a
log sentinel rather than after a pipe; the seven skips are the same seven classes as the previous SHA
and none is new. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, bare `mypy` over 217 files, `drift_guard` and
`doc_budget` all exit 0. No frozen file is in the delta; 0 non-ASCII and 0 CR measured byte-wise on
the blobs rather than with a CR grep.

**WHAT REMAINS, stated rather than rounded up.** In a shared worktree NEITHER lane can release, so
records leak there - bounded, because the next claim clears a record whose cycle ended, and it is the
declared cost of refusing to guess. A row wedges alongside a wedged lane when a stale lock cannot
prove its holder; the escape is documented and CS-1010 carries the behaviour that would take neither
harm. The driver renders the new refusal as `lane_held` because it never reads the reason - CS-1011.
NO REAL LANE NIGHT HAS RUN: every measurement here is processes and locks driven directly, never a
driver fired end to end.

### 2026-09-12 - CS-987 - CLOSED. The bind-failure arm's leak oracle asked a process-global question and attributed the answer to the call under test, so it went RED on a correct refusal and would have gone GREEN on the leak it exists to catch

**WHAT CLOSED.** `tests/surface/test_server.py::test_run_exits_non_zero_on_a_bind_failure_and_binds_nothing_else`
ended with a population question - every thread whose name contains `serve`, summed over
`threading.enumerate()`, asserted to be zero. `threading.enumerate()` is PROCESS-wide, one
xdist worker runs many modules in one process, and `clockspeed/surface/server.py` names its
serving thread `clockspeed-serve`. So a SUCCESSFUL `server.run` anywhere in that worker left
a daemon satisfying the filter for the rest of the process's life, and the arm read a
neighbour's residue as its own leak.

**HOW IT WAS FOUND, and it was not a read.** A whole-suite run on the CS-964 merge candidate
under `-n auto` went red on gw3 at `assert 1 == 0` while everything the arm is actually about
BEHAVED: the bind failed as designed, the exit was `EXIT_BIND_FAILED`, and the refusal printed
naming the port and `OSError 10048`. Because `-x` was in effect the red stopped the whole
suite at 3048 passed, which is a tier-1 cost on its own.

**THE FALSE RED WAS THE LESSER FAULT.** A population question cannot tell the subject's own
leak from a neighbour's live thread in one direction, nor from a neighbour's already-exited
thread in the other. On a run where no sibling had served yet it reported 0 whether or not
the subject leaked. It could not observe the value it was asked about, which is the one way
an arm passes for no reason at all.

**THE REPAIR.** The set of thread IDENTITIES is taken before and after the call and the
assertion is on what APPEARED. Identity rather than name, because a name is not unique and a
neighbour may start another thread sharing one.

**WHAT WAS REFUSED, and why each would have left the defect.** Narrowing the FILTER instead -
excluding daemon threads, matching the name harder, or marking the arm serial - each leaves
the oracle asking a global question and merely shrinks the population able to answer it. The
false green survives all three. The written fence in the item note said so before the repair
was attempted, and the repair did not depart from it.

**PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is what the acceptance required.**

- POSITIVE: a leak planted in `server.run`'s bind-failure path - a thread named
  `clockspeed-serve-LEAKPLANT` started before the refusal returns - reddens BOTH arms, and the
  failure message names the planted thread. The plant was asserted to have LANDED before the
  run, from a script written with a file-writing tool after a quoted heredoc silently ate the
  backslashes out of the matched source line and the resulting unmutated run reported green -
  a mutant that never applied and a surviving mutant produce identical output.
- NEGATIVE: `test_the_leak_oracle_ignores_a_serving_thread_this_call_did_not_start` holds a
  foreign `clockspeed-serve` thread alive for its whole duration and stays GREEN. It also
  asserts the NAIVE population oracle still SEES that thread, so the arm measures the
  difference between the two questions rather than restating one of them. Reverting that
  arm's oracle to the population question reddens it.

**HOW TO VERIFY INDEPENDENTLY.** `python -m pytest tests/surface/test_server.py -q -p no:randomly`
reports 131 passed. The arm and its control are `test_run_exits_non_zero_on_a_bind_failure_and_binds_nothing_else`
and `test_the_leak_oracle_ignores_a_serving_thread_this_call_did_not_start`. The sibling grep is
clean and was part of the close: `threading.enumerate()` appears at exactly ONE site across
`tests/`, `clockspeed/` and `tools/`, so there is no population to repair beside it.

**THE ITEM WAS FILED AND CLOSED IN THE SAME SESSION**, which is recorded rather than hidden:
it was filed when it blocked a merge verdict, and repaired the same day because
`.githooks/pre-push` runs the suite with `-x`, so a nondeterministic cross-test red could
block every push in the project until it was fixed.

### 2026-09-11 - CS-980 - THE (14,60) PROPERTY WALL WAS OURS, NOT THE FORMAT'S. Every payload of the pinned world now decodes, and a documented gate's premise is refuted

**What changed.** `clockspeed/save/objects.py` gained a third dispatch on the version pair,
beside the two it already had for the body prefix width and the transform delta. The pair
carries a different tag grammar: one lead byte between the payload head and the first tag,
a recursive type NAME where the legacy shape has a type word plus tag-extra strings, and a
flags bitfield where the legacy shape has a guid flag. Merged files
`clockspeed/save/objects.py` and `clockspeed/save/world.py`, verified by
`tests/save/test_property_payload_14_60.py` against a synthetic fixture in
`tests/save/synthetic.py`, so the arm runs on a machine with no game and no save.

**WHY IT WAS LOOKED AT AT ALL, recorded because the trigger matters more than the fix.**
The operator demonstrated a third-party tool rendering container contents and miner
settings out of a save on this machine while this project decoded zero property tags from
the same file. `CLAUDE.md` section 8 says ground truth beats every document; `docs/GATED.md`
was the document, and it lost.

**WHAT THE GATE SAID AND WHY IT WAS WRONG.** CS-G05 recorded that every record of every
`(14,60)` save decodes zero property tags and that such a save "cannot exercise the decoder
at all - it is the CONTROL", cause unestablished between payload framing and value grammar.
The zero was real and reproduced on demand. The inference from it was not: a save that
decodes nothing under ONE grammar is not a save that carries nothing. The answer was
framing AND grammar, which is why neither candidate alone closed it.

**THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, since a plausible fix and a correct one look alike here.**
Four readings were driven against the whole record population and compared: the lead byte
alone left every container value unreachable; the lead byte plus a guid-flag reading broke
hundreds of records, almost all on `StructProperty`; a sixteen-byte struct guid was worse
still; the flags bitfield read every record with no breaks. One bit's width rests on two
tags and is recorded as weak. A bit never observed refuses the payload rather than assuming
a width - non-negotiable 7.

**WHAT IT UNBLOCKS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.** Every walked payload of the pinned development
world now reads, and container values, object references and integers are published where
none were. Struct INTERIORS are deliberately still not read: CS-829 owns that, and carrying
a new grammar into the interior reader in the same change would have made one measurement
answer for two. So an item total is still not derivable, and the reason is now a narrower
and named one - see CS-981.

**A SECOND ARM WENT VACUOUS AND WAS NARROWED RATHER THAN DELETED.**
`tests/save/test_properties.py::test_save_60_refuses_the_grammar_the_other_pairs_accept`
still passes and its zero is still true, because the sweep it runs carries its own
independent reader of the LEGACY grammar. Its DOCSTRING claimed the save reached a
terminator on no payload at all, which ground truth refutes. The claim is now stated as
what it measures - the legacy reader must go on refusing this pair, or the two grammars
have converged and the dispatch between them grades nothing. The symbol was deliberately
NOT renamed: `docs/LEDGER.md` and `docs/history_notes.md` cite it by name and both are
append-only, so a rename would rot two citations in records that are never edited.

**The license gate that ran first is the entry above this one.** No third-party source was
copied, and the two refused candidates - including the tool the operator demonstrated -
were not read. The grammar above was derived from the bytes of saves on this machine.

### 2026-09-11 - CS-980 - LICENSE GATE RESULT. Five third-party save parsers triaged before a byte of format knowledge entered the tree, and the one the operator watched is the one that is refused

**This entry closes nothing.** It records the `CONVENTIONS.md` section 14 gate that had to
pass before the CS-980 decode work could consider an external format reference, per the
rule that the gate result is recorded BEFORE the project acts on it. Retrieved 2026-09-11.

**Why the gate ran.** The operator demonstrated satisfactory-calculator.com's interactive
map rendering container contents and miner settings out of a save on this machine, while
this project's own reader decodes zero property tags from the same file. That makes a
third-party parser the obvious hypothesis generator and therefore a license question.

**The project's own license was read, not assumed:** `LICENSE` is the MIT License,
copyright line `Copyright (c) 2026 Clockspeed contributors`. It is a frozen file under
`CLAUDE.md` section 6, so any inbound term that attaches to the whole work conflicts with
it and is refused without a verbal clearance being available.

**Per-candidate verdicts.**

- `AnthorNet/SC-InteractiveMap` - **REFUSED for every purpose, including reading.** No
  LICENSE file, GitHub reports no license, `package.json` carries no `license` field and is
  marked private. Its README states that reuse of the source and data assets is not
  permitted in any case and that the source is available for educational purposes only -
  wording that reaches past copying toward a derived independent implementation, so the
  safe default is refusal. It is very probably the code behind the map the operator
  watched, which makes it the most tempting candidate and the most clearly fenced. Its
  repository root also carries a third party's save file, so cloning it would import one.
- `etothepii4/satisfactory-file-parser` - **CLEARED WITH OBLIGATIONS.** MIT,
  `Copyright (c) 2021-2025 etothepii`, notice-retention and warranty paragraphs both
  present, manifest and license agree. Reading requires nothing. Lifting any portion would
  require reproducing the MIT text and that copyright line in a third-party notices file.
  It does NOT relicense this project. Its README states GAME versions, never numeric save
  versions - the version pair mapping stays this project's own pin.
- `ficsit-felix/ficsit-felix` - CLEARED WITH OBLIGATIONS (MIT, holder bitowl), but
  format-stale and therefore low value.
- `GreyHak/sat_sav_parse` - **REFUSED, including for reading.** GPL-3.0. Copyleft bars
  vendoring absolutely, and it is written in this project's own language, which carries the
  highest structural-copying risk of any candidate.
- `FabianFG/CUE4Parse` - reading CLEARED WITH OBLIGATIONS, vendoring REFUSED. Apache-2.0
  with an unfilled template copyright line and a NOTICE naming twenty-plus upstreams
  including a path into Epic's engine source. A clean license that is not vendor-safe.
- `moritz-h/satisfactory-3d-map`, its save-format document - reading CLEARED WITH
  OBLIGATIONS, copying REFUSED. The repository is GPL-3.0,
  `Copyright (C) 2021 - 2026 Moritz Heinemann`, and the document carries no separate grant,
  so the prose is covered by it. Not one sentence, field-name table or list may enter this
  tree. It is nonetheless the only current document found that addresses the decode
  question at all.
- `satisfactorymodding/Documentation` - UNRESOLVED and therefore refused for copying. No
  license file at the repository root and the license endpoint returns 404. Absence is not
  permission. It adds no byte-level fact.

**The wiki's save-format pages, re-measured.** They still do not cover the body of the
version pair this project parses: the page states the body has not been analyzed beyond
Patch 1.0.0.3. It now names header version 14, but as a header-only note. The byte this
project already measured false is still labelled with a name implying a meaning the bytes
do not carry, now annotated as unused garbage - which partially converges with
`BOOTSTRAP.md` section 2.4 and still refutes any flag reading of it. CS-485's verdict and
`CLAUDE.md` section 7's no-lifted-datasets fence are unchanged and were not re-litigated.

**The operative distinction, recorded because this project has conflated it before.**
Reading a source to learn a byte layout and then writing an independent implementation is
not what MIT, Apache-2.0 or GPL-3.0 attach obligations to - their duties attach to
distributing copies or conveying a derivative. Copying a line, a table, a constant list or
a fixture is a different act with a different answer per license, and under GPL-3.0 it
would relicense this project and conflict with the frozen `LICENSE`.

**The standing instruction this puts on the decode work.** Restate every adopted fact in
this project's own words and confirm it against the local bytes before it becomes code. The
always-legal path is the one CS-482 already used - derive the grammar from the saves on
this machine with a structural anchor, with any cleared reading serving only as a
hypothesis generator. No test fixture from any candidate may be copied under any license;
the synthetic-fixtures settled entry and non-negotiable 11 bar it independently of this
gate.

**No save file, no fragment of one and no hex dump of one was uploaded, pasted or
submitted anywhere during this gate.** All retrieval was outbound fetches of public
repository metadata and documents.

### 2026-09-11 - CS-970 - CLOSED. The lane names why it refused, and no night that accomplished nothing reports success

**Two acceptance clauses were AMENDED, and this record is the amendment.** The
adjudicator required the change be written down rather than inferred from its verdict,
because an agent that rewrites its own acceptance after the fact is how an acceptance
stops being a fence.

- `ROADMAP.md` asked for a test driving the DIRTY-WORKTREE precondition. No such check
  exists anywhere in `ops/loop/lane_launcher.py`: `ensure_worktree` returns early once
  `.git` is present and runs no git at all on a reused worktree. The ROADMAP line itself
  labelled that reading "unproven". A clause cannot require an arm for a precondition with
  no code, so the arm drives the real lock-repoint refusal instead. Adding a dirty-tree
  check was considered and REFUSED: a dirty lane worktree is normal between cycles, and
  refusing it would convert a recoverable state into a permanently dead lane.
- `ROADMAP.md` asked for ELEVEN identical consecutive launch failures to stop the driver.
  The driver stops at THREE. Eleven was the count observed in the incident, not a designed
  threshold, and three matches the existing consecutive-error precedent. Stopping sooner
  discharges the clause strictly.

**What shipped,** across `aa5a828`, `6814f90`, `e3276bb`, `6bad0e4` and `03bcf1c`. Merged
files: `ops/loop/lane_launcher.py`, `ops/loop/queue_loop.py`, `tests/test_lane_launcher.py`,
`tests/test_queue_loop.py`. A closed thirteen-member `LAUNCH_REASONS` vocabulary, one
path-free code per raise site; the driver validating an incoming code against its OWN copy
and rendering its own literal by index; a consecutive-launch-failure stop with its own exit
code; a no-push cycle recorded as a verdict and refused by the roll-up; and a progress
counter that stops any night which never produces a commit. Verified by
`tests/test_lane_launcher.py::test_every_launch_error_raise_site_names_a_reason`,
`::test_every_raise_site_keeps_the_reason_code_it_was_reviewed_with`,
`tests/test_queue_loop.py::test_the_driver_and_the_launcher_hold_the_same_reason_vocabulary`,
`::test_the_launch_fault_row_never_renders_the_caller_s_object`,
`::test_a_night_that_never_completes_a_cycle_cannot_run_the_full_budget` and
`::test_a_night_committing_to_the_lane_branch_runs_its_whole_budget`.

**THE SUITE WAS GREEN AT EVERY REFUTED COMMIT.** Four adversarial rounds landed findings
against trees that had just passed 6224, 6241 and 6256 tests. Round 1: `lane_held` reset the
counters, so a night whose lock was held every cycle ran all twelve and exited 0. Round 2: a
COMPLETED cycle that pushed nothing did the same; a budget at or below the limit exited 0;
and an unlisted stop word read as success through a `.get(stopped, EXIT_OK)` default. Round
3: the progress test read the `ok` roll-up, which is false on a no-push cycle, so a worker
following `tools/headless-queue.md`'s own instruction to push the LANE BRANCH on a rejected
push had its night killed at cycle 3 - a REGRESSION this work introduced, worse than the
burn it was written to stop. THE PATTERN IS THE FINDING: the same defect reappeared four
times wearing a different field each time, and only an allowlist over what counts as
progress, rather than a denylist of what does not, finally held.

**A PRIVACY GUARANTEE THAT WAS NEARLY TRUE.** The driver validated the reason by VALUE and
then rendered the CALLER'S OBJECT, so a `str` subclass whose data is honestly a vocabulary
member but whose `__str__` returns a home path was written verbatim into the durable JSONL
row. Two adversaries broke it by different mechanisms. Never reachable in the field, since
every raise site binds a module constant, but the fix is structural: `type(reason) is str`
plus an index substitution, so this module renders only its own literal. Either defence
alone is insufficient.

**THIS FILE'S OWN 2026-09-11 RECORD IS CORRECTED.** The entry above states that CS-970's
eleven consecutive failures "were a launcher meeting a bare repository". That cannot be the
mechanism. Every failing cycle left a 134-byte worker log containing the `lane start` header
that `ops/loop/run_lane.ps1` writes, and a bare-repository fault raises in `ensure_worktree`
BEFORE any worker is spawned, so no log would exist at all. The runner started every time and
died before writing its exit line. The trigger remains UNDIAGNOSED.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE.** No arm calls `launch_lane` through to a real spawned worker;
every arm injects seams. Eleven of the twelve reasons could be recorded WRONG in the field
with the suite green. If the lane is re-armed and cycle 2 fails as before, the row will most
likely read `runner_exited_early` or `spawn_failed`, naming the proximate mechanism and
sending the reader to the runner rather than to the contended tree. The work makes the next
failure self-describing; it does not make the lane start.

**RESIDUALS, all filed rather than left implicit.** CS-974 holds the `_CI_ROLLUP_BAD`
denylist, under which a cancelled, skipped, timed-out, unavailable or unknown CI verdict
still rolls up as a good cycle. CS-975 holds the fact that nothing reads the driver's exit
code at all, so `EXIT_NO_PROGRESS` and `EXIT_UNKNOWN_STOP` are decorative in production.
Accepted and not filed: a worker that advances HEAD with a junk commit reads as progress,
and the site-to-code mapping arm encodes a reviewed reading rather than ground truth.

**Independently verified** at `03bcf1c` in a worktree pinned to that SHA, tree confirmed
unmoved at both ends: `pytest tests -q -n auto --dist loadfile` exit 0, 6262 passed, 7
skipped; `mypy` exit 0, 189 source files; `ruff check .` exit 0; `tools/drift_guard.py` exit
0, 11 guards, 10 PASS, 1 WARN, 0 FAIL, the WARN being CS-971's ROADMAP budget;
`tools/doc_budget.py` exit 0, VERDICT WARN, 1 soft failure. Every behavioural claim was
